content.value_statement: Teams need current guidance when building on Neon Serverless Postgres. This skill routes Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to official Neon setup, API, and operations references.
actual_capabilities: Points agents to official Neon documentation and markdown reference pages.
Explains Neon setup, projects, branches, endpoints, and connection strings.
Compares TCP, HTTP, WebSocket, edge, serverless, and long-running connection patterns.
Covers Neon CLI, MCP, REST API, TypeScript SDK, and Python SDK workflows.
Guides use of branching, autoscaling, scale to zero, restore, replicas, pooling, and IP allow lists.
Covers Neon Auth and Neon JS data API integration topics.
limitations: It is a documentation routing skill, not a live Neon account integration.
It cannot inspect projects, databases, logs, or billing without separate authorized tools.
It should fetch current Neon docs before giving version-sensitive guidance.
It does not replace Neon security review for production database changes.

use_cases.description: Plan safe use of Neon CLI, MCP, REST API, and SDK workflows for infrastructure tasks.

use_cases.title: Design Database Environments
use_cases.description: Use branching, restore, replicas, pooling, and allow lists for development, testing, and production workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Neon Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain what Neon Serverless Postgres is and when I should use it. Include projects, branches, endpoints, and compute behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Pick My Driver
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the best Neon connection method for my runtime. My app runs on [runtime] and needs [query pattern].

prompt_templates.title: Plan Preview Branches
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Neon branching workflow for preview deployments, schema migration testing, and cleanup after pull requests close.

prompt_templates.title: Design API Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Neon CLI, MCP, REST API, TypeScript SDK, and Python SDK for automating project, branch, and endpoint management.

output_examples.input: I am building a Next.js app on Neon and need database access from serverless routes.
output: The response recommends checking current Neon connection docs first.
It compares HTTP and WebSocket patterns for serverless runtimes.
It notes when pooling helps with bursty concurrency.

output_examples.input: I need isolated databases for every preview deployment.
output: The response explains Neon branches as copy-on-write environments.
It outlines creation, migration testing, and cleanup steps.
It points to Neon CLI or MCP workflows for automation.

output_examples.input: I want to manage Neon resources from a Python service.
output: The response routes to Neon Admin API and Python SDK guidance.
It covers API key handling, operation polling, and rate-limit awareness.
It recommends confirming current SDK behavior in the official docs.

best_practices: Fetch current Neon documentation before answering version-sensitive questions.
Choose the connection method based on runtime, transaction needs, and concurrency.
Use branches and restore features for safer testing before production changes.
anti_patterns: Do not guess Neon URLs when the docs index can identify the correct page.
Do not recommend production changes without confirming plan limits and access controls.
Do not expose connection strings, API keys, or database credentials in prompts or examples.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps agents answer Neon Serverless Postgres questions using official setup, driver, API, and operations references.

faq.question: Can it manage my Neon account directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only. Account management requires separate authorized tools or Neon interfaces.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover Neon Auth?
faq.answer: Yes. It points to Neon Auth and Neon JS guidance for authentication and data API workflows.

faq.question: Does it cover production operations?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers autoscaling, scale to zero, restore, replicas, pooling, allow lists, and logical replication topics.

faq.question: Should agents rely only on the skill text?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs agents to verify current details against official Neon documentation.
